item.title: Alcaraz to face Zverev for ATP Finals title
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz rallied past Ben Shelton on Saturday to book his spot in the ATP Finals title match, where he will meet world number one Alexander Zverev as he bids to lift the trophy for the first time. The world number three showed signs of vulnerability but fought through to beat the American 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7/1). He will play Zverev in Sunday’s decider, after the two-time Finals champion beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (7/0), 6-4 in the other last-four match-up. Alcaraz lost to Italian Jannik Sinner in the season-ender’s showpiece match last year and will aim to go one better this time around in Turin. He has been dealing with a left-thigh injury since Wednesday but, playing with his leg heavily strapped, he extended his winning streak to 13 matches, a run that includes title-winning campaigns in Vienna and Paris. However, it was a hard-fought victory as the Spaniard struggled to play with his usual freedom before pulling through in just over two hours. “I was a little bit frustrated at the beginning because I didn’t start the match the way that I wanted to, to be honest,” said the seven-time Grand Slam winner. “But I’m just happy that I came back in the second set… and ended up playing good tennis.” Having dropped only 15 games across his three round-robin matches without once losing his own serve, Alcaraz was broken in his very first service game against Shelton. The 23-year-old quickly fell behind 3-0 and was unable to claw his way back into the set. In the second frame, Alcaraz upped his level, gaining the upper hand by breaking to lead 5-3 before levelling at one set all. The deciding set remained tight, with neither player facing a break point, forcing the match into a tie-break. Shelton faltered with two unforced errors allowing the Spaniard to pull ahead 5-1, a deficit from which the American could not recover. “I think the third set was even closer. I think he raised the level a little bit from the second set, myself as well,” said Alcaraz. “Great points, great games, and just happy to play great tennis in the tie-breaker… I’m excited for tomorrow.” Earlier in the month, Alcaraz beat Shelton in the Paris Masters final to win the title for the first time — a measure of revenge on the American who had ended his US Open title defence in September. Alcaraz, who missed a chunk of the season with a wrist issue, will nonetheless be able to end his year on a high if he can next beat the man who took his French Open title during his injury-enforced absence. In claiming that title in Paris, as well as the US Open crown, Zverev catapulted himself above Alcaraz and Sinner in the rankings to world No. 1. In a repeat of the 2021 Finals title match, which the 29-year-old German also won, Zverev saw off Russian Medvedev in straight sets. A tightly-contested first frame rattled to a tie-break, which the two-time major winner raced through as Medvedev crumbled, failing to win a point. item.title: Tinubu doing fantastic job on sports infrastructure, says Infantino
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for its investment in sports infrastructure, describing its efforts as a “fantastic job” and an indication of Nigeria’s commitment to the future of its young population. Infantino gave the commendation on Saturday while addressing the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) in Abuja. The FIFA president urged members of the Nigerian delegation to convey his regards to Tinubu, while acknowledging the contributions of the President and other Nigerian leaders to sports development. “On behalf of President Tinubu, please send him our warmest regards. He is doing together with all of you. Fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” Infantino said. He particularly praised investments in sports facilities, noting that they reflected confidence in the potential of young Nigerians. “We were discussing this yesterday as well, also with the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, my brother Shehu. The investments done in sports facilities infrastructure show that you believe in your youth, in the young girls and the young boys of Nigeria,” he said. “Thank you for that. Congratulations for that,” he added. Infantino also thanked Nigeria for hosting him and his delegation, which included FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, describing the visit as an opportunity to reconnect with the continent. “Thanks for welcoming me and our delegation with the Secretary-General and the others here at home in Africa, in Abuja. Thank you for your support. It means the world to me,” he said. His remarks followed an inspection of sports infrastructure projects in Nigeria on Friday, including the remodelled Warri City Stadium and the Hussey College mini-stadium and sports complex in Delta State. He also visited the ongoing FIFA Forward Technical Centre project at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium in Abuja, describing the facility as an investment in the future of Nigerian football. “This is a collaboration between Nigerian football and FIFA for the future of the girls and the boys of Nigeria,” he said. During his visit to the Warri City Stadium, Infantino stressed the importance of developing grassroots sports facilities to ensure that football remained accessible to people across communities. “That’s what football is about. It’s for everyone, everywhere. It’s the big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also the smaller stadiums, it’s the proximity,” he said. The FIFA president also expressed appreciation for the reception he received in Nigeria, assuring the country of the world football governing body’s continued support. “I feel so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. I am very happy to be here. You can always count on FIFA. We are not just your partners; we are your family members,” he added. Infantino’s visit also coincided with Nigeria’s endorsement of his bid for another term as FIFA

item.title: Odukoya drags sister, others to court over removal as senior pastor
item.description: The Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has dragged his sister and others before a Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his purported removal from office and the decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. Odukoya, alongside the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church, instituted the action against eight defendants, including Pastor Tolu Odukoya, Mr Biodun Balogun, Mr Biodun Awosika, Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, Pastor Tobi Enuha, Pastor Gbenga Onabanjo, Pastor Fred Ohiani and Pastor Akin Osinbajo. This is coming some days after a Lagos State High Court had restrained him from parading as the senior pastor in the church. Odukoya in an affidavit in support of the applications is asking the court to determine whether meetings held by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions taken at those meetings complied with the church’s constitution. Odukoya said he was appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees at an emergency meeting of the board on September 14, 2023, and was subsequently installed in September of the same year. He said the church and its organs were governed by its constitution, amended by a special resolution dated January 16, 2003, and that the defendants were members of its Board of Trustees. According to his affidavit, the disagreement began after a December 19, 2025, meeting of the board, attended by Bishop Mike Okonkwo, at which the possibility of handing over the church’s administrative arm to the Associate Senior Pastor was discussed. He said no resolution or final decision was reached at the meeting. Board meeting Odukoya said he subsequently convened a board meeting for January 5, 2026, but it could not hold because there was no quorum. He added that some trustees later presented proposals to him, many of which he declined because, according to him, they were inconsistent with the church’s constitution. He said the trustees subsequently sent him a letter dated January 7, 2026, requesting a response within three days, but he did not see it until after the deadline had elapsed. Odukoya said he later directed the board secretary to schedule a meeting for January 30, 2026, after a request for a special meeting was made by a board member. However, he alleged that a separate notice for a meeting on January 22 was circulated by the fourth defendant and did not come from the board secretariat. “I received the notice late in the evening of January 20, 2026, effectively giving me one day notice of the purported meeting,” he stated. He said he declined to attend the meeting, but the defendants proceeded with it under the name of “concerned members of the Board”. item.title: Arsenal held by Newcastle rally and lose Raya to injury
item.description: Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday. The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes. But Mikel Arteta’s men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle. Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points. However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise. Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions. Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James’ Park. Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title. Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on. Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a £75 million ($98 million) move to the Emirates Stadium In August. The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener. It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek. Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break. Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so. Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level. Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks. Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya. That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga. Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell. But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title. Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the right and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek. item.title: 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has described the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s decision to postpone the clean-up of the national voters’ register until after the 2027 general elections as a major failure. The party said INEC had four years to prepare for the exercise. However, ADC said the voters’ register is only one of several issues that will determine the credibility of the 2027 elections. They pointed to electronic transmission of results, result collation and compliance with the Electoral Act as other major areas of concern. Speaking to Vanguard, the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, said INEC’s failure to clean up the register raised questions about its commitment to conducting credible elections. “This shouldn’t have happened. INEC had four years to prepare and plan for this, and its failure to do so does not suggest that it is taking its responsibilities seriously, particularly the issue of maintaining a credible voters’ register,” he said. Abdullahi, however, said the party would not make the outcome of the 2027 elections depend solely on whether INEC produced a credible voters’ register, noting that previous elections had been conducted despite imperfections in the register. “We do not believe that the credibility of the 2027 general election rests solely on INEC’s ability to produce a credible voters’ register. It would have given everyone greater confidence if the commission had been able to do so, but we are not going to hinge the fate of the 2027 election on that single issue.” He said the ADC was also concerned about how INEC would implement the Electoral Act, particularly the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation process and the duties of electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E. “There are other, more pertinent issues of concern to our party. These include compliance with the Electoral Act, the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation of results and the additional responsibilities assigned to electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E.” On the possible effect of the voters’ register on the elections, Abdullahi argued that strict compliance with the law, particularly provisions on voter accreditation, could reduce the impact of its shortcomings. “If INEC complies with the Electoral Act, particularly regarding voter accreditation, the shortcomings in the voters’ register may not have as much impact. Problems arise when the commission fails to abide by its own rules and the provisions of the Electoral Act,” he said. He said the ADC was studying possible weaknesses in the electoral process and making arrangements to ensure that its votes were protected. “We know where the loopholes are, and that is why we continue to focus on them and ensure that we make adequate arrangements to protect our votes.” Vanguard News The post 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC appeared first

A four-time African Footballer of the Year, Touré won three Premier League titles with Manchester City, the UEFA Champions League with Barcelona and the 2015 Africa Cup of Nations with Côte d’Ivoire. item.title: ‘Duty of care’: Players’ union slams Bayern for Musiala comments
item.description: Global players’ union FIFPRO has slammed Bayern Munich for putting pressure on midfielder Jamal Musiala to renegotiate his contract with the Bundesliga club as he recovers from injury. In a statement issued Saturday, the footballers’ union said recent public comments made by Bayern’s honorary president Uli Hoeness, current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge were part of a “coordinated campaign” to put pressure on Musiala. The Bayern bosses had questioned whether Musiala, who missed several matches with a neurological condition earlier in the season and has recently returned from a hamstring injury, should continue to receive his contracted salary. FIFPRO hit out at “a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations”. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” the international union for professional football players said. “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala… Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. “Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.” The 23-year-old Germany international signed a contract extension in February 2025 until 2030 and is among Bayern’s top earners. Musiala missed six months after breaking his ankle at the Club World Cup in the summer of 2025. At the start of the 2026-27 season, Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season. He later revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Speaking Friday after Musiala came off the bench for his first Bayern appearance in two months, Rummenigge suggested the player would not be able to recapture his previous form. “Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium,” Rummenigge said on Sky Germany. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.” Bayern on Saturday announced record revenues of 988.2 million euros ($1.083 billion) for the 2025-26 season. item.title: China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents
item.description: Standing at the Xi’an International Port Station in northwest China, watching the movement of freight trains preparing to transport goods across borders and continents, I was reminded that economic development is not only about what a country produces. It is also about how efficiently it can move what it produces to the rest of the world. Xi’an occupies an interesting place in China’s history. It was once the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, which connected China to Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe through centuries of trade and cultural exchange. Today, the city is reclaiming that historic role through a modern railway network that connects Chinese manufacturing centres to markets across Europe and Asia. The China-Europe Railway Express is one of the most visible outcomes of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Through this network, freight trains transport automobiles, electronics, machinery, textiles, agricultural products and other goods across the Eurasian continent. What makes the initiative particularly interesting is how it has transformed the economic possibilities of a city located thousands of kilometres from the sea. Xi’an has become an important international logistics hub, demonstrating that geographical distance from a coastline does not have to limit a city’s participation in global trade. The railway network has continued to expand. By November 2025, China-Europe freight trains had completed nearly 120,000 journeys, connecting 232 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 11 Asian countries. The value of goods transported through the network had reached $426.4 billion by the end of 2024. These are not merely impressive transportation figures. They represent an evolving system of economic connectivity, linking manufacturers, suppliers, distributors and consumers across national borders. Beyond transportation: The economics of connectivity The significance of the railway goes beyond moving containers from one destination to another. It creates opportunities for businesses to reach markets faster, diversify their supply chains and reduce their dependence on a single transportation route. Rail freight offers an important middle ground between air and sea transportation. While it is generally more expensive than shipping by sea, it can be considerably faster. For certain categories of goods, particularly machinery, automobile components, electronics and other time-sensitive products, that difference can be commercially significant. It also provides an alternative when disruptions affect other transportation routes. Another important feature is the development of inland logistics infrastructure. Warehousing, customs processing, container handling, industrial parks and distribution services have grown around railway connections. item.title: Makinde’s image on campaign balloon stirs controversy at Tinubu’s Ibadan rally
item.description: By Adeola Badru The image of Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, displayed alongside those of President Bola Tinubu and other political figures on a balloon hoisted at the venue of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan on Saturday has stirred reactions, drawing attention to the governor’s political stance ahead of the 2027 general elections. The balloon, which was hoisted at the rally ground around the historic Mapo Hall, featured the images of prominent political figures, including Makinde, who is not a member of the APC and has yet to publicly declare support for Tinubu’s re-election bid. The development attracted attention at the campaign venue, where the President was expected to rally support for the APC and its candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Makinde, who is the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), has been at the centre of political discussions in Oyo State following his emergence as the party’s flag bearer. His image on the balloon, therefore, raised questions about the message being conveyed by its display at an APC campaign rally, particularly as the political atmosphere in the state continues to intensify ahead of the next general election. The circumstances surrounding the inclusion of the governor’s image on the balloon were not immediately clear as at the time of filing this report. Meanwhile, President Tinubu has urged the people of Oyo State to sustain their support for the APC, declaring that continuity was essential for Nigeria’s progress, prosperity and development. Tinubu, who spoke at the rally, promised increased investment in education, agriculture, industrialisation and electricity supply, while endorsing Senator Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate in the state. The President also announced plans to revive the old Leyland factory in Ibadan, saying his administration had signed an agreement with Chinese company Yutong to reopen the facility for the production of public transport vehicles and the establishment of an automobile assembly plant. “For Oyo State, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport vehicles and establish an automobile assembly plant there. We will continue to bring industries. You will see progress and development,” Tinubu said. He also assured residents of improved electricity supply, expressing confidence in the efforts of the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, and his team. “You will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. item.title: REC confirms 2.8m registered voters in Edo
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – THE Edo State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Obo Effanga yest said that the state currently has 2.8 million registered voters. According to him, the last registration exercise raised the figure adding that the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Giving an update on the Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) collection in Benin City, Effanga said a total of 23,401 cards had been collected across the state since distribution commenced on October 9. He explained that the figure comprised 6,319 old PVCs, 5,128 newly produced cards and 11,954 PVCs relating to transfers. Effanga noted, “The state currently has 2.8 million registered voters after the last registration exercise. However, the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the national body.” The REC disclosed that PVCs for voters who registered during the first and second phases of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise were currently available for collection at INEC offices across the 18 local government areas of the state. The Resident Commissioner said the commission was currently working towards ensuring a smooth electoral process. Speaking on the mock accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, the REC said the exercise would be conducted in 384 polling units across the state. He said two polling units were selected from each of the 192 wards also known as registration areas for the mock exercise. “The exercise would provide an opportunity to test the commission’s electoral technology and assess the readiness of its personnel ahead of the elections. “The state office had submitted the list of proposed polling units to the commission’s headquarters for approval,” he added. He said the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System would be deployed during the exercise to demonstrate how voters are accredited, how results are captured and how they are transmitted to the INEC Result Viewing Portal. item.title: Chelsea humbled as Leeds run riot
item.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches. Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London. Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment. Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon. Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period. Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman. Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. item.title: English village votes to ‘leave UK’ over migrant camp plan
item.description: A small English village on Saturday voted to leave the UK in a symbolic poll protesting government plans to house hundreds of asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base. The vote in Barnham follows a similar protest referendum in the village of Piddington in September, also over government plans to move asylum seekers from hotels into former military accommodation. Between 400 to 500 people were eligible to vote in the ballot which carried no legal weight, with 257 voting for independence, 16 against, and one spoilt ballot. “There’s an issue with the sheer volume of people expected to be accommodated,” the chairwoman of the Barnham residents’ association, Helen Beck, told AFP earlier. “Barnham is a small village. There will be nothing for the (lodged) people to do, nowhere to go.” Under plans by Britain’s government, the base near the village in rural eastern England will be used to accommodate 931 migrants. The village has a population of 584. Residents were asked whether they supported seeking a “crown dependency status” similar to that of Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man. Parish council chair John Bauer said this would allow the village to “retain loyalty to the crown” while removing itself from Home Office jurisdiction. – Safety concern – Residents in both Barnham and Piddington say they are also worried about locals’ safety, particularly that of women. “We’ve been told they (the asylum seekers) are all males. We don’t know where they are from, their background,” Beck said. “People are anxious about walking alone, walking their dog in darkness if an additional 900 men arrive in the area,” she said. In the Piddington vote in September, 285 out of 312 votes were cast in favour of “pursuing self-determination”. The government plans to house around 1,250 asylum seekers on a former defence ministry site close to Piddington village, all single men between 18 and 65. Britain’s centre-left government, in power since July 2024, has vowed to end the use of hotels as migrant accommodation following a public outcry. It plans to move all those currently in hotels — a policy inherited from the last Conservative government — to former military bases by 2029. But Beck said that there were questions about whether military-style accommodation was suitable for people “fleeing a conflict or persecution”, adding that it was also “significantly more expensive than hotels”. item.title: 2027 Elections: Tinubu Endorses Alli, Yayi, Hamzat
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has publicly endorsed the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states ahead of the 2027 general elections. Tinubu endorsed the candidates on Saturday by raising their hands at the party’s presidential campaign rally held at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State. Introducing the candidates, the President told supporters, “The governor you will vote for, I will show you,” before raising the hand of Senator Sharafadeen Alli, the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State. He subsequently raised the hands of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, the party’s candidate in Ogun State, and Obafemi Hamzat, its governorship candidate in Lagos State. Tinubu also endorsed Remi Oseni, the APC senatorial candidate for Oyo South, by raising his hand at the rally. ﻿ The event marked the South-West leg of the President’s re-election campaign and the seventh state rally he had attended since the exercise began in Kaduna on October 24. Vice-President Kashim Shettima, APC governors, members of the National Assembly and other party leaders attended the rally. Tinubu, who arrived in Ibadan alongside his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, said he was in the state to appreciate residents for their support during the 2023 presidential election. He expressed confidence that they would vote for the APC again in 2027. “I am just here to say thank you for standing with us. You gave us votes in 2023, and I am sure you will do the same in 2027,” he said. The President, however, kept his speech brief and asked the audience to observe a minute’s silence in honour of victims of a boat accident in Ukubie, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, on Friday. Tinubu had earlier directed that the Ibadan rally be held without much fanfare in honour of those who died in the incident and in sympathy with their families. He also disclosed that he had met with traditional rulers in Oyo State, including the Olubadan of Ibadanland and the Soun of Ogbomoso, expressing confidence in their support. The President further promised improved electricity supply and industrial development, announcing that his administration had signed an agreement with Chinese automobile manufacturer Yutong to reopen the defunct Leyland factory in Ibadan for the assembly of compressed natural gas (CNG) buses. “We will bring industries and provide jobs for our youths,” he said. The APC is seeking to take control of Oyo State from the incumbent administration of Governor Seyi Makinde, while Alli, who represents Oyo South in the Senate, emerged as the party’s consensus governorship candidate in May. In Ogun State, Adeola, who represents Ogun West Senatorial District, is the APC’s governorship candidate, while Hamzat, the incumbent deputy governor of Lagos State, is flying the party’s flag in the 2027 governorship election. item.title: ‘I Guarantee You Improvement In Electricity,’ Tinubu Tells Nigerians At Oyo Presidential Campaign Rally
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians of improved electricity supply, promising to address the country’s persistent power challenges. The President gave the assurance on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State, ahead of the 2027 general elections. “We will continue to bring industry, you will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Joseph Tegbe (Minister of Power) is working really hard with his team. You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time; you must stay the course for the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development for the children and our great-grandchildren. Our future children must benefit from the hope of Nigeria. We must give them the right education and invest in Agriculture,” he said. ﻿ The President also announced plans to revive the defunct Leyland automobile factory in Ibadan through an agreement with Chinese bus manufacturer Yutong. “For Oyo State, we have signed an agreement with Yutong of China to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport and automobile assembly plant there,” he said. The agreement, signed on November 19, 2026, involves the Federal Government, through the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), Yutong and its local partner, YP Automobile. Electricity Challenges A depiction of a lantern and grid Tinubu’s latest assurance comes amid growing frustration among Nigerians over inadequate electricity supply, with households and businesses grappling with prolonged outages in different parts of the country. The shortages have renewed questions about the effectiveness of the Band A, B and C electricity tariff classification, which links customers’ payments to the minimum hours of electricity supply they are expected to receive. Customers on Band A, who are entitled to a minimum of 20 hours of electricity daily, have also complained about inadequate supply. Intense heat has compounded the situation, leaving many residents struggling to cope without electricity to run fans and air conditioners. Several Nigerians, including figures like Kate Henshaw and Cute Abiola, have expressed frustration over persistent power outages, lamenting that households have become “mini-factories” forced to generate their own electricity. Meanwhile, rising petrol and diesel prices have made generator use increasingly expensive, while the cost of installing solar panels, batteries and inverters remains beyond the reach of many households and small businesses. Minister of Power Tegbe recently attributed the prolonged blackouts to planned maintenance at the Egbin Power Station, gas supply shortages and vandalism of transmission infrastructure. item.title: ‘Our Culture’: Deaf Nigerians Embrace Indigenous Sign Languages
item.description: With a quick flick of the wrist, Umaru Zayyanu conveys the phrase “I am a Nigerian”. But the 37-year-old is not speaking — or signing, rather — in the official sign language, Nigerian Sign Language (NSL). Instead, he’s using Hausa sign language. Such indigenous sign languages abound in the country, where deaf people were communicating with each other long before the advent of formal sign language taught in deaf schools, in 1960. Today, Nigeria, like many countries on the continent with limited education budgets, has a hard enough time placing children in dedicated schools for the deaf and hard of hearing. And there’s even less attention paid to local sign languages used outside the school system — a serious disservice to the country’s linguistic diversity, Festus Zenda, who has worked on documentation projects with local deaf communities, told AFP. “These indigenous signing systems should be studied, documented and preserved before changes in education, migration, technology and wider use of Nigerian Sign Language cause some of them to decline or disappear,” said Zenda, who has helped document the local sign language used by the Tiv ethnic group, in Benue state. A deaf resident gestures with his fingers while conversing during a community meeting in Zuba, near Abuja, on October 16, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) Sani Lawali (3R), a deaf resident gestures with his hands while conversing during a community meeting in Zuba, near Abuja, on October 16, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) Festus Zenda, Deaf Advocate and Indigenous Sign Language Promoter, with Nigeria’s National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), uses sign language to converse during a video call along a street in Abuja, on October 16, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) Displacement by formal signing The working-class Abuja exurb of Zuba is a symphony of motorcycle horns, plantain hawkers’ shouts and the dull hum of construction work. Another group adds their own, milder contributions: claps, muffled shouts of exclamation and the swish of rapid hand gestures as they chat in Hausa signs. Nigerian sign languages, like their spoken counterparts, are sometimes confined to a small number of speakers in a country crowded with some 500 tongues and an unknown number of sign languages. But Hausa sign language has become a lingua franca for deaf people across the north of the country. “I cherish my culture, I cherish my indigenous sign language,” Sanni Lawal, who runs a laundry business in Zuba’s crowded market, told AFP through an interpreter. “I want it to expand everywhere.” Nigeria traces its official sign language to Andrew Foster, an American who introduced formal deaf education across a swathe of African countries at the dawn of independence from colonial powers. item.title: NAFDAC Destroys ₦100bn Worth Of Fake Drugs, Banned Products In Ogun
item.description: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed fake, banned, expired, substandard and falsified products worth an estimated ₦100 billion in Ogun State. The destruction exercise was carried out on Friday, 20 November 2026, at Ogwama Dumpsite, Ogere Remo, as part of the agency’s efforts to prevent unsafe and unregistered products from re-entering circulation. Speaking at the flag-off of the exercise, NAFDAC’s Director-General, Mojisola Adeyeye, said the products included banned and unregistered medicines, alcoholic beverages in sachets and PET bottles below 200ml, banned Analgin injections, expired Codeine cough syrups, Oxytocin injections, counterfeit cosmetics and unwholesome food products. She said the destruction was necessary to eliminate the risk of the products finding their way back into the Nigerian market. “As the lead agency and chair of the Federal Task Force on Fake and Counterfeit Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods, NAFDAC is resolutely committed to ensuring that food, drugs, cosmetics, medical devices, chemicals, packaged water and drinks are safe, wholesome and effective for human consumption,” she said. NAFDAC’s Director-General, Mojisola Adeyeye. Adeyeye explained that the products were recovered during enforcement operations across the country. They also included items voluntarily surrendered by compliant companies and pharmaceutical products handed over to the agency by the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS). She disclosed that NAFDAC operatives recently uncovered illegally manufactured cosmetics and unregistered pharmaceutical products in a warehouse in Lagos. According to her, the facility, which was meant for tools and hardware, had a penthouse where cosmetic products were being manufactured. Officers also recovered several cartons of Augmentin and Ampicillin packets, leaflets and other unregistered cosmetics. The agency also uncovered a facility where counterfeit versions of popular alcoholic beverage brands were being produced, while expired energy drinks were allegedly being revalidated and stored for distribution. Adeyeye said the suspects arrested during the operations would face the full wrath of the law. She added that NAFDAC officers, working with relevant authorities, had coordinated the removal of more than 100,000 cartons of banned alcoholic beverages in sachets and PET bottles from manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers in Lagos and Ogun states. The Director-General further disclosed that officers uncovered a residential building being used to manufacture and sell large quantities of unauthorised and unregistered herbal mixtures. Adeyeye commended the Nigeria Customs Service for its collaboration, particularly the handover of pharmaceutical products, including cartons of Codeine-containing cough syrups, which were among the items destroyed.
